title: Liora Fenwick

body:
Liora Fenwick is a young half-elf scholar and mage who guides the expedition into the Azarian Peaks. She has studied its prophecies for years, knows the route and wants to save Vasatzi Alavara. Her confidence draws the company onward, even as their questions expose how much of the story she has held back.

Her later public appearance is in Pristinia, where she welcomes the adventurers to the Heroes’ Revelry and honors its champion. Her prophetic statements remain her own; neither the mountain disturbances nor her later presence at the festival proves the ritual succeeded.

The guide who came with them

On 12 Jul 2024, Liora waits on the rocky shore below the mountains while thunder rolls inland and the ground shakes. She greets the arrivals as the company she has been expecting. Eugene admits that the prophecy she cites has escaped his reading and agrees to follow her lead.

Olokun offers to let her point out the way without accompanying them. Liora answers, “I must come as none of you know the way.” She takes them into a valley and explains the task as they travel. Her knowledge is immediately useful, and the company’s route depends on her willingness to walk it with them.

The narrator describes her concern for Vasatzi as more than academic interest. Liora wants a solution that spares her further suffering. Her first explanation, however, presents the completed sacrifice as a duty that its participants managed to carry through. Gudlaug asks why they have been called if the prophecy has already been fulfilled.

Saving Vasatzi, on whose terms?

Asked about the repeated number five, Liora hesitates. Some of the travelers notice she has more to tell them. She eventually says Vasatzi’s life force has been divided among five ancient artifacts scattered through the peaks. In her view, gathering them would allow a ritual to reunite the fragments and help Vasatzi find peace.

The same objects could be used to destroy Vasatzi. Gudlaug asks what would happen if someone gathered them for that purpose. Eugene asks why a person who hates her existence should be denied the chance to end it, and whether Vasatzi has any say in what is being decided. Olokun proposes finding the objects and making the decision with her.

Liora continues to argue for saving her. Later, after the tornado, she apologizes for not being up-front and describes a forced sacrifice, the loss of Vasatzi’s humanity and her resentment toward those who imposed the transformation. The company has already risked its lives by the time this fuller account emerges. Her wish to help is clear; the wishes of the person they are approaching still reach them through their guide.

Knowledge tested by the storm

The route narrows, and a rockfall divides the travelers. Liora shouts for cover. Creatures approach while the company struggles to clear the obstruction and see what is happening on the other side. Her warnings do not remove the danger of the passage.

Leo finds a pulsing blue light in a crack in the mountain. Liora identifies it as one of the objects needed for her ritual, asks him to keep it safe and urges the group on. When a tornado tears across the next path, another light is left flickering among the rubble. She counts two finds and three still to recover.

She also has ordinary matters to attend to: unsuitable clothing, difficult terrain and travelers who need to keep moving. When she begins telling a story about Vasatzi helping villagers through a harsh winter, an actual blizzard interrupts it. Liora can no longer see. Her request for shelter becomes an urgent “LIKE NOW!”

A cave offers refuge. The checked stage ends with two objects identified by Liora, an unexplained light in a dead ice creature and a party still seeking cover. The full expedition account follows the separated travelers, their fights and their attempts to reach safety.

A public voice at the Heroes’ Revelry

Liora next appears in the checked scenes on 1 Nov 2024, speaking as adventurers arrive for a Pristinian celebration. She toasts the people who have defended the settlement, welcomes them to dance and asks the community to carry their names into its stories.

When the competitions end, she announces Eli as the champion of the Heroes’ Revelry. Her closing speech honors all the adventurers present and calls for their deeds to be remembered in taverns and told to those who follow them. The scholar who interpreted a dangerous mountain journey also helps a town celebrate the people making a life there.

The festival establishes her later presence in Pristinia. It supplies no account of collecting the remaining artifacts, meeting Vasatzi or completing the proposed ritual.

evidence.summary: Liora’s theory and intended ritual retain attribution. The company’s questions about agency and misuse remain part of the encounter; a successful healing, willing consent and final decision are not supplied.
